findings.issue: The capacity shortfall has been stated but not fixed. The spec's own figures for core work to 13 Nov are P14 21.0, P15 12.0, P13 about 30.5 and P16 about 10.5 person-days. That totals about 74 person-days against a nominal 34 (17 working days x 2 students), before P01-P12 and P17 are counted. I re-checked the sums against the local r3 packets and they are correct. The cross-packet plan is still marked UNRESOLVED. The first-run notice promises to 'show the later date', but no later date is named. M09 also needs starter-graph T0 modules from other packets by 6 Nov. An entrant cannot know when the tool becomes usable.
findings.fix: Before 23 Oct, publish one table covering all packets: module, owner, person-days, and the date each core slice lands. Then pick one of two options. (a) Cut core to the never-cut minimum across all packets so that it fits 34 person-days. (b) Set a dated 'reliable from' day for entrants (for example 20 Nov) and print it on the first-run notice now. The M09 pilot date must follow whichever date is chosen.

findings.module_id: Cross-packet (P15-M03/M06 vs P16-M03; P15-M02 vs P16-M04)
findings.issue: The packets define two incompatible status vocabularies and two run-provenance records, and P15 flags neither conflict. P16-M03 (r3, read locally) defines five statuses: verified, team assumption, unverified, unresolved and FALSE ASSUMPTION as a terminal marker. Its rules are also different: verified needs a recorded reviewer, team assumption needs a named owner, and a result takes the worst input. P15-M03 defines four statuses {verified, team_assumption, unverified, false}, treats 'unresolved' as a workflow state, and counts verified as satisfied by 'at least one opened source'. P16-M04 records runs as PROV-O JSON-LD with a 'by/proposer/reviewer' field. P15-M02 records runs as an RFC 8785 RunRecord with decided_by {code|ai|person}. The 'single status vocabulary' metric therefore holds only inside P15. Node chips would disagree with the P16 ledger and exports.
findings.fix: Name one owner for the status enum and one for the run record. Adopt one schema, for example P16-M03's statuses mapped onto P15's chips, with decided_by as a projection of PROV agents. Add a cross-packet contract test that fails when the two enums or field names diverge. Record the overlap in P15's flags.

findings.module_id: P15-M07 vs P13-M06v vs P16-M04 (board export)
findings.issue: Three packets now own board JPEG export, and their methods conflict. P15-M07 specifies a lossless allow-list segment rewriter so that pixel data is never re-encoded. P13-M06v validates the boards. P16-M04 (r3) 're-encodes panels as JPEG without metadata (sharp)' and draws superseded marks into the pixels. That is the lossy route P15 rejected, and it changes the file hash, which invalidates P15's 'scan passed' stamp bound to post-strip hashes. P15 flags only P13 and P14.
findings.fix: Choose one export pipeline with a fixed order: render marks, then a single re-encode if one is unavoidable, then the lossless strip, re-scan and stamp, all at the last step. Give it one owner and one stamp format. Add P16-M04 to the overlap flag.

findings.issue: The meta-tag CSP does not govern dedicated workers loaded from same-origin URLs. The spec's own source P15-S18 says workers take their CSP from the header on their script response. Only blob and data workers inherit the creator's policy. The core host is unnamed, and on GitHub Pages it cannot send headers. The T0 evaluator worker and the P14-M07 parser workers, which hold Layer 0 geometry, would therefore have unrestricted fetch, WebSocket and importScripts. A compromised dependency inside a worker could send design data out, and nothing would stop it. Separately, script-src lacks 'wasm-unsafe-eval'. Any WebAssembly in the document context (rhino3dm, web-ifc or manifold-3d in P14 core) would be blocked, so the CSP will either break Layer 0 import or be loosened ad hoc.
findings.fix: Name a header-capable host for core, such as Cloudflare Pages _headers, and send a CSP header on every worker script. Alternatively, start every worker from a blob: URL so that it inherits the document policy, and add blob: to worker-src. Add 'wasm-unsafe-eval' to script-src. Run P14's importers under the CSP in CI. Add a CI test that calls fetch, WebSocket and importScripts from inside each worker and expects denial.

findings.issue: jsep's default '^' is bitwise XOR at precedence 4. That is below the comparisons (7), + and - (9), and * and / (10). Only '**' (11) is right-associative. If the spec's grammar operator '^' is evaluated as a power, 'a + b^2' parses as '(a+b)^2', and 'x^2 >= 9' parses as 'x^(2>=9)'. T0 threshold formulas would return wrong numbers without any error, and these formulas are the main way modules compute pass/fail. jsep's defaults also include ||, ??, &, |, shifts, %, Compound, SequenceExpression, this, member access and array literals. The allow-list walker must reject all of them.
findings.fix: Call jsep.removeBinaryOp for every unlisted operator. Either use '**' for power or re-add '^' with addBinaryOp('^', 11, true). Define how unary minus binds relative to the power operator (-2^2). Add precedence fixtures, for example 'a+b^2', '2*a^2' and 'x^2>=9', each with an expected value. Have the evaluator reject every jsep node type outside the grammar.

findings.module_id: P15 packet (course rule: code / AI / person)
findings.issue: The packet breaks its own decided_by rules. M03 says 'no ai-drafted value is verified without a named person's confirmation'. Yet four metrics are marked status and evidence_status 'verified' with decided_by role ai and confirmed_by null: M01 keyboard operability, M01 non-text contrast, M02 scheduling cost, and M05 published registry size. M03 also requires decided_by on 100% of parameters, but most non-numeric parameters carry none, for example connection_rule, cycle_policy, storage_model and the licence rules.
findings.fix: Downgrade those four to team_assumption, or record a named student's confirmation with a pseudonym and date. Add decided_by to every parameter. Run the M03 lint over this packet and publish the pass/fail count in the change log.

findings.issue: This was an r3 condition and is only partly met. Twelve metrics still carry status 'false_assumption_corrected', a value outside the four-value enum. The packet's own 'Single status vocabulary' lint would reject them. The note explaining that 'status' is a history marker is an exception the schema does not allow.
findings.fix: Set status equal to evidence_status on every metric. Move 'false_assumption_corrected' into history[] entries of the form {was_false_in, corrected_in, evidence}.

findings.issue: The spec says 'Whether React Flow pans focused nodes into view is undocumented'. The ReactFlow API reference, opened 21 Oct 2026, lists autoPanOnNodeFocus with default true. The drag/gesture enumeration also omits panActivationKeyCode (default 'Space', Space+drag pans) and zoomOnDoubleClick. React Flow's accessibility page also uses Space to select a node.
findings.fix: Cite autoPanOnNodeFocus and test whether the auto-pan clears the Controls, MiniMap and panels. If it does not, use setCenter with padding. Add panActivationKeyCode and zoomOnDoubleClick to the Playwright prop enumeration, and decide whether the Space key conflicts with node selection.

findings.issue: Event Timing reports per event, not per interaction. A single click produces pointerdown, pointerup and click entries. Taking 'p98 over all scripted interactions' from raw entries double-counts interactions and mixes event types.
findings.fix: Group entries by interactionId and take the maximum duration per interaction before computing p98. Keep the 16 ms floor for interactions with no reported entry.

findings.issue: Cancel relies on Worker.terminate, but first-party module code may run on the main thread ('first-party code or the T0 evaluator in a worker'). A long first-party node cannot be cancelled, which breaks the 'Progress and cancel coverage' metric.
findings.fix: Require every evaluation node, first-party included, to run in a worker in core, or exclude main-thread nodes from the over-10 s class with a measured bound.

verdict: Not passable. Round 4 fixed most r3 items: pseudonymous actors, the lossless JPEG rewriter, the T0 hardening design, licence notices and the drag inventory. Entrants still cannot rely on the tool. Core work across all packets needs about 74 person-days against 34, and no dated fallback is given. P15 and P16 define conflicting status vocabularies, run-provenance records and board-export pipelines; P16's lossy re-encode would invalidate P15's hash stamp. The meta CSP does not cover same-origin workers, which hold Layer 0 data, and it lacks wasm-unsafe-eval. jsep's default '^' is XOR at low precedence, so T0 formulas would compute wrong values without any error. The packet fails its own lint: invalid status values, and AI-drafted 'verified' metrics with no confirmation. The Layer 0 freeze owner is still unnamed.
